audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 at a 47.83% win rate is right: Karma owns level 1 and gets a breather at 6, and loses every stage where Riven's dashes and Ki Burst are up.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2 was marked Skill in both layers while its own why says her second Q dash plus Ki Burst 'cross your Q range and lock you down before Inspire can shield it'.
audit.why: Level 2 is the stage where Riven first has a gap-close plus the stun; nothing about it is contested. The packet levelChart gives it to Riven.
audit.corrected: Row 1 flipped to Riven in matched pairs, rating dropped to 3/10. The other six rows already agreed with the packet and with their whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: The tracked ability's cooldown was never given, and dosFull[2].d claims a whiffed Ki Burst buys 'the fifteen-second invitation'. Ki Burst is 11/10/9/8/7 seconds — at rank 5 that is under half the stated window.
audit.why: The whole page tells the player to commit on Ki Burst's downtime, so an inflated number gets them killed by a stun that is already back. The real interaction chain — bait E Valor's shield-dash first so the Focused Resolve tether cannot be broken — is already correct in the mid text and wants.you[2].
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and report[5].t now carry the real 11/10/9/8/7-second cooldown.

edits.before: The stun glues her combo together — bait it before fighting. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Ki Burst is 11/10/9/8/7s and glues her combo together — bait it, then fight on its downtime.

edits.before: Riven burns Ki Burst (Stun) on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Riven burns Ki Burst on nothing — you have up to eleven seconds to punish.

edits.before: Track Riven’s Ki Burst (Stun): The stun glues her combo together — bait it before fighting. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Riven’s Ki Burst: 11/10/9/8/7 seconds, and it glues her combo together — bait it before you fight her.

notes: Riven's Ki Burst cooldown was overstated as fifteen seconds; it is 11/10/9/8/7, which matters because the entire page keys commits to its downtime. Level 2 was the only chart row out of step with both the packet and its own why. Unverified and left alone: the existing description of Wind Slash as an 'execute' — Riot's text only says it is a powerful ranged attack usable once. The full layer also calls Riven 'his' in several inherited template strings; that is a page-wide pronoun issue, not edited here.
